amc8-ajhsme-1994-01.title: Compare with one half
amc8-ajhsme-1994-01.body:
All are below $\frac12$. How far below? $\frac12-\frac5{12}=\frac1{12}$ is the smallest gap ($\frac12-\frac38=\frac18$, $\frac12-\frac13=\frac16$, ...). So $\frac5{12}$ is largest.

**Answer: (D) $\dfrac{5}{12}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-03.title: Add the total time
amc8-ajhsme-1994-03.body:
She is at work $8$ h $45$ min including lunch. $7{:}25$ A.M. $+\ 8$ h $=3{:}25$ P.M., plus $45$ min $=4{:}10$ P.M.

**Answer: (C) 4:10 P.M.**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-03.title: Before and after lunch
amc8-ajhsme-1994-03.body:
From $7{:}25$ to noon she works $4$ h $35$ min, leaving $3$ h $25$ min. Lunch ends at $12{:}45$, and $12{:}45+3{:}25=4{:}10$ P.M.

**Answer: (C) 4:10 P.M.**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-04.title: Move each shape
amc8-ajhsme-1994-04.body:
$120^\circ$ is one third of a turn. Clockwise, the shape at the top (triangle) moves to the lower right, the shape at the lower right (square) moves to the lower left, and the shape at the lower left (circle) moves to the top. That is: circle on top, square lower left, triangle lower right: (B).

**Answer: (B)**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-04.title: Follow one shape
amc8-ajhsme-1994-04.body:
The circle is at the lower left. A clockwise third of a turn moves the lower-left position to the top. Only (B) has the circle on top, and its other shapes match too (square lower left, triangle lower right).

**Answer: (B)**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-05.title: Unit fractions
amc8-ajhsme-1994-05.body:
$1\text{ mile}\times\frac{8\text{ furlongs}}{1\text{ mile}}\times\frac{40\text{ rods}}{1\text{ furlong}}=320$ rods.

**Answer: (B) 320**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-06.title: A 2 and a 5
amc8-ajhsme-1994-06.body:
Any six consecutive whole numbers include a multiple of $5$ and an even number. So the product is a multiple of $10$ and ends in $0$.

**Answer: (A) 0**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-06.title: Example
amc8-ajhsme-1994-06.body:
$1\times2\times3\times4\times5\times6=720$ ends in $0$; the argument above shows this always happens.

**Answer: (A) 0**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-07.title: Two triangles
amc8-ajhsme-1994-07.body:
In triangle $ABE$: $\angle ABE=180^\circ-60^\circ-40^\circ=80^\circ$. Since $A, B, C$ are on a line, $\angle DBC=180^\circ-80^\circ=100^\circ$. In triangle $BDC$: $\angle BDC=180^\circ-100^\circ-30^\circ=50^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $50^\circ$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-07.title: Exterior angle
amc8-ajhsme-1994-07.body:
$\angle DBC$ is an exterior angle of triangle $ABE$, so it equals $60^\circ+40^\circ=100^\circ$. Then $\angle BDC=180^\circ-100^\circ-30^\circ=50^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $50^\circ$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-08.title: Digit sets
amc8-ajhsme-1994-08.body:
Three digits at most $9$ summing to $25$ are $9,9,7$ or $9,8,8$. Each set gives $3$ arrangements: $997, 979, 799$ and $988, 898, 889$. Total $6$.

**Answer: (C) 6**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-08.title: Shortfall from 27
amc8-ajhsme-1994-08.body:
The digits fall short of $9+9+9=27$ by $2$ in total: either one digit is $2$ short ($3$ choices) or two digits are each $1$ short ($3$ choices). $6$ numbers.

**Answer: (C) 6**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-09.title: Step by step
amc8-ajhsme-1994-09.body:
$20\%$ off: $80$ dollars. Coupon: $75$ dollars. Tax: $8\%$ of $75$ is $6$. Total $81.00$ dollars.

**Answer: (A) 81.00 dollars**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-10.title: Divisors of 36
amc8-ajhsme-1994-10.body:
$N+2$ must be a divisor of $36$ that is at least $3$. The divisors are $1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36$; dropping $1$ and $2$ leaves $7$, giving $N=1,2,4,7,10,16,34$.

**Answer: (A) 7**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-10.title: Count pairs
amc8-ajhsme-1994-10.body:
$36$ has $9$ divisors. $N\ge1$ means $N+2\ge3$, which excludes $1$ and $2$: $9-2=7$.

**Answer: (A) 7**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-11.title: Through Jonas
amc8-ajhsme-1994-11.body:
Jonas has $40$ students, $20$ of them girls, so $20$ Jonas boys. The other $52-20=32$ boys are from Clay.

**Answer: (B) 32**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-11.title: Through Clay girls
amc8-ajhsme-1994-11.body:
Girls from Clay: $48-20=28$. Clay has $60$ students, so Clay boys: $60-28=32$.

**Answer: (B) 32**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-12.title: Use side length 2
amc8-ajhsme-1994-12.body:
Give each big square side $2$ (area $4$).
- I: two right triangles with legs $1$ and $1$: $\frac12+\frac12=1$.
- II: one $1\times1$ square: $1$.
- III: two small tilted squares, each with diagonals of length $1$, so area $\frac12\cdot1\cdot1=\frac12$ each: $1$.

All three shaded areas are equal.

**Answer: (A) The shaded areas in all three are equal.**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-12.title: Fractions of the square
amc8-ajhsme-1994-12.body:
I: each shaded triangle is half of a corner quarter-square, so $\frac18$; two of them make $\frac14$. II: one of four equal squares, $\frac14$. III: the lines cut the square into $16$ congruent small triangles, and the shaded part is $4$ of them, $\frac14$. All equal.

**Answer: (A) The shaded areas in all three are equal.**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-14.title: Child-minutes
amc8-ajhsme-1994-14.body:
Two children play for $90$ minutes: $180$ child-minutes. Shared by $5$ children: $36$ minutes each.

**Answer: (E) 36**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-14.title: Fraction of the time
amc8-ajhsme-1994-14.body:
At any moment $2$ of the $5$ children play, so each plays $\frac25$ of the time: $\frac25\times90=36$.

**Answer: (E) 36**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-15.title: Repeat every 4
amc8-ajhsme-1994-15.body:
The path repeats every $4$ points: from a multiple of $4$ it goes right, up, right, down. $425=4\times106+1$ behaves like point $1$: from $1$ the arrows go up to $2$, then right to $3$. So from $425$: up, then right: (A).

**Answer: (A)**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-15.title: Compare with 1 to 3
amc8-ajhsme-1994-15.body:
$424$ is a multiple of $4$, at the bottom like $0, 4, 8$. Then $425$ is like $1$, $426$ like $2$, $427$ like $3$. The arrows $1\to2\to3$ are up then right.

**Answer: (A)**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-16.title: Scale the sides
amc8-ajhsme-1994-16.body:
Perimeter $3$ times as large means each side is $3$ times as long, so the area is $3\times3=9$ times as large.

**Answer: (E) 9**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-16.title: Example
amc8-ajhsme-1994-16.body:
Sides $1$ and $3$: perimeters $4$ and $12$ (ratio $3$), areas $1$ and $9$ (ratio $9$).

**Answer: (E) 9**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-17.title: Running total
amc8-ajhsme-1994-17.body:
Snow: $4\times10\times3=120$ cubic yards. Totals after each hour: $20, 39, 57, 74, 90, 105, 119$. After $7$ hours only $1$ cubic yard remains, which takes a few more minutes. Closest: $7$ hours.

**Answer: (D) 7**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-17.title: Average rate
amc8-ajhsme-1994-17.body:
Over about $7$ hours her average rate is about $17$ cubic yards per hour, and $120\div17\approx7$.

**Answer: (D) 7**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-18.title: Match each part of the trip
amc8-ajhsme-1994-18.body:
The graph should rise slowly (city), then steeply (highway), stay flat for an hour (shopping), drop steeply (highway), then drop slowly (city). Graph (B) has a gentle rise, a steep rise, a flat top, a steep drop and a gentle drop.

**Answer: (B)**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-18.title: Eliminate
amc8-ajhsme-1994-18.body:
(C), (D), (E) have no flat part, so Mike would never stop at the mall. (A) has constant speed on each leg, with no slow city part. Only (B) fits.

**Answer: (B)**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-19.title: Add the radii
amc8-ajhsme-1994-19.body:
Each semicircle has radius $2$ and bulges $2$ beyond its side. A side of $ABCD$ touches the far point of a semicircle, so $ABCD$ extends $2$ beyond the original square on every side. Its side is $2+4+2=8$ and its area $64$.

**Answer: (E) 64**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-19.title: Through the centre
amc8-ajhsme-1994-19.body:
The distance from the centre of the original square to a tangent side is $2$ (half the square) $+\,2$ (the radius) $=4$. So $ABCD$ has side $8$ and area $64$.

**Answer: (E) 64**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-20.title: Small tops, big bottoms
amc8-ajhsme-1994-20.body:
Use the smallest digits $1, 2$ as numerators and the largest $8, 9$ as denominators. Two ways: $\frac18+\frac29=\frac{9+16}{72}=\frac{25}{72}$, or $\frac19+\frac28=\frac{8+18}{72}=\frac{26}{72}$. The smaller is $\frac{25}{72}$.

**Answer: (D) $\dfrac{25}{72}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-20.title: Pair the bigger numerator with the bigger denominator
amc8-ajhsme-1994-20.body:
The larger numerator $2$ does less damage over the larger denominator $9$. So $\frac{1}{8}+\frac{2}{9}=\frac{25}{72}$.

**Answer: (D) $\dfrac{25}{72}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-21.title: Worst case
amc8-ajhsme-1994-21.body:
With bad luck you could get $3$ of each colour, $9$ gumballs, without four of one colour. The $10$th gumball must make four of some colour. So $10$.

**Answer: (C) 10**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-21.title: Pigeonhole
amc8-ajhsme-1994-21.body:
With $10$ gumballs and $3$ colours, some colour has at least $\lceil10/3\rceil=4$. With $9$ it can fail ($3+3+3$).

**Answer: (C) 10**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-22.title: Both even or both odd
amc8-ajhsme-1994-22.body:
First wheel: $3$ fills half, $1$ and $2$ a quarter each. So $P(\text{even})=\frac14$, $P(\text{odd})=\frac34$. Second wheel: $4, 5, 6$ in thirds: $P(\text{even})=\frac23$, $P(\text{odd})=\frac13$.

$P(\text{sum even})=\frac14\cdot\frac23+\frac34\cdot\frac13=\frac16+\frac14=\frac{5}{12}$.

**Answer: (D) $\dfrac{5}{12}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-22.title: Equal-sized outcomes
amc8-ajhsme-1994-22.body:
Split the first wheel into $4$ equal parts: $1, 2, 3, 3$. With the second wheel's $3$ parts there are $12$ equally likely pairs. Even sums: $1+5$, $2+4$, $2+6$, $3+5$, $3+5$: $5$ of $12$.

**Answer: (D) $\dfrac{5}{12}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-23.title: Write the sum
amc8-ajhsme-1994-23.body:
The sum is $111X+(10Y+X)+X=113X+10Y$. For a $3$-digit sum we need $113X+10Y\le999$. With $X=8$: $904+10Y\le999$ allows $Y=9$, giving $994$. ($X=9$ would give at least $1017$.) $994$ has digits $9, 9, 4$ = $Y, Y, Z$ with $Z=4$ (different from $X=8$, $Y=9$). Form $YYZ$.

**Answer: (D) $YYZ$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-23.title: Check the addition
amc8-ajhsme-1994-23.body:
$888+98+8=994$. ✓ The digits are $Y=9$, $Y=9$, and a new digit $4$, so the form is $YYZ$.

**Answer: (D) $YYZ$**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-24.title: Green spreads up and right
Count by number of greens
amc8-ajhsme-1994-24.body:
$0$ greens: $1$ way. $1$ green: only the top-right ($1$). $2$ greens: top row, or right column ($2$). $3$ greens: all but bottom-left ($1$). $4$ greens: $1$. Total $6$.

**Answer: (B) 6**

amc8-ajhsme-1994-25.title: Use 10^94 − 1
amc8-ajhsme-1994-25.body:
$\underbrace{99\ldots9}_{94}=10^{94}-1$, so the product is $\underbrace{44\ldots4}_{94}\underbrace{00\ldots0}_{94}-\underbrace{44\ldots4}_{94}=\underbrace{44\ldots4}_{93}3\underbrace{55\ldots5}_{93}6$. Digit sum $=93\cdot4+3+93\cdot5+6=372+3+465+6=846$.

**Answer: (A) 846**
